svg.aria-label: Three columns: the administrator holds the Dropbox login, a copy of the folder key, the game's admin password; a host holds a copy of the same folder key and their own game password; the folder holds the copies with password hashes and the On Air token. A strip lists what a stolen key gives and does not give.
svg.text: Administrator
• Dropbox login: makes and changes the keys
• a copy of the folder key, in the vault
• the game's administrator password:
pairing codes, accounts
• the launcher's "I set the table up" flag
(a local flag, not checked anywhere)
Admin buttons: New token, Pair a launcher,
Change the keys, Ask to hand over
Host
• a copy of the same folder key, in the vault
• their own game password
• no Dropbox account at all
Can technically do everything in the folder.
Cannot change the keys (needs the login).
Hosting is a trust decision: keep the
hosts few, usually just the Game Master.
Folder
• the game, every copy: kingdom, map,
journal, accounts with password hashes
(salted PBKDF2, never the passwords)
• the images
• the On Air token (the address's key)
• who hosts, from which PC
Not here: the session-cookie secret,
the Dropbox password, any other file
A stolen folder key
Gives: read everything, now and later; upload a doctored copy the next Start loads; delete copies; with the token, sit at the table's address with a fake page.
Does not give: the Dropbox account, any other file in it, the passwords in clear, the hosts' PCs, a logged-in session.
Remedy: disconnect the app on dropbox.com (kills every copy), authorise again, New token, a code per host. The launcher warns when another program sits at the address.
